why.text: Cool, humid summers with little sun ripen the grapes slowly. Acidity ends higher than in other zones.

styles.text: Dry whites, rosados and reds. Berezia wines are aged for at least 5 months in tanks of cement, ceramic or wood.

climate.text: Atlantic, humid and mild, with cool summers. About 1,200 mm of rain and 1,710 hours of sun a year.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to straw; balanced, fresh; white fruit, citrus, herbs; slightly bitter finish. Rosés: raspberry to salmon pink. Reds: violet red to picota; balanced, tannic. Berezia adds spice, balsamic and toast.

styles.name: Aparta Berezia
styles.text: Made by special methods such as skin contact; pale yellow to amber or orange.

styles.name: Berezia
styles.text: Aged at least 5 months in tanks; spice, balsamic, nuts and toast.

why.text: Stony, slate-rich soils on steep slopes drain rainwater well. Winters are cold and summers very hot.

styles.text: Young reds and whites. Both can also be aged in oak.

climate.text: Continental Mediterranean: winters down to -10 °C, summers above 30 °C, six months of frost, less rain than elsewhere in Asturias.

soil.text: Stony soils on slate and schist, acidic but near neutral (pH 6), on steep slopes.

tastes.text: Reds: ruby to cherry red; wild red berries; fresh, light tannin. Aged reds add balsamic, spice and toast. Whites: pale yellow to greenish; stone fruit, white flowers, citrus, mineral. Aged whites add spice and toast.

why.text: Vines by the sea, 1,600 mm of rain and dry southerly winds late in ripening give a fresh, light txakoli.

styles.text: Almost all white, fresh and light with a slight fizz. Rosado and red are rare. Barrel-fermented white is also made.

climate.text: Mild Atlantic with sea influence: 1,600 mm of rain, mean 13.4 °C, 1,800 hours of sun. No spring frost risk.

soil.text: Hard limestone and sandstone alternate with soft marl and clay rock. Loam and clay-loam textures, usually neutral pH.

tastes.text: Whites: pale green-yellow to gold; fresh green fruit, herbs; fine fizz, slightly bitter finish. Rosés: pink to fuchsia; citrus, mint. Reds: garnet; black pepper, then blackberry, raspberry. Barrel whites: new wood.

styles.name: Txakoli blanco fermentado en barrica
styles.text: White fermented in barrel; golden, balanced, new wood notes.

why.text: Atlantic climate, 170 days of south wind and a mean of 13.1 °C give round txakoli with citrus and herbal flavours.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, usually dry. Berezia versions are aged at least 5 months. Semi-dry and sweet styles are also allowed.

climate.text: Atlantic: mean 13.1 °C (highs 18.7, lows 7.5), about 899 mm of rain and south wind on 170 days a year.

soil.text: Soil pH about 5.2 to 8.2, with active limestone.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to straw; green apple, tropical fruit, citrus; lightly acidic, slight prickle. Rosés: pale pink to salmon; red fruit. Reds: black cherry, violet tints; green pepper, berries. Berezia adds spice, nuts and toast.

styles.name: Berezia
styles.text: Aged at least 5 months in wood, ceramic or cement; spice, nuts, toast.

why.text: Mild, humid Atlantic climate and poor, thin, acidic soils, with vines on pergolas. Wines are known for their acidity and aroma.

styles.text: Mostly white, Albariño above all. Reds are less common. Oak-aged whites are sold as Barrica. Quality sparkling wine is also made.

climate.text: Marked Atlantic and mild (10 to 25 °C), with about 1,300 mm of rain a year, much less in summer.

soil.text: Mostly granite, with some schist and river sediments. Sandy, acidic, poor in nutrients and fairly thin.

tastes.text: Albariño: straw yellow with gold or green tints; citrus, floral, apple; light acidity, good structure. Barrica: golden; toast, smoke, vanilla. Reds: picota with violet tints; red fruit; moderately tannic.

styles.name: Rías Baixas Albariño
styles.text: White of great aromatic complexity: citrus, floral and apple.

styles.name: Rías Baixas Barrica
styles.text: Oak-aged white: golden; toast, smoke, vanilla and dried fruit.

styles.name: Rías Baixas Espumoso
styles.text: Sparkling: fine, persistent bubble; fresh and lightly acidic.

why.text: Steep terraces on slate and granite rise above the Miño and Sil canyons. The climate is more continental than Atlantic, with long hot summers.

styles.text: Reds, whites and rosados, usually young, some aged in barrel; Mencía leads the reds, Godello the whites.

climate.text: More continental than Atlantic: long hot summers, mild autumns, 700 to 800 mm rain, mean 11.3 °C, strong winds.

soil.text: Alluvial soils over slate, with granite in places. Acidic, and riverbank soils hold little moisture.

tastes.text: Reds: cherry to purple red; red berry or stone-fruit aromas; balanced. Whites: pale to golden yellow; white tree fruit. Rosés: pale pink to cherry; wild berries. Barrica wines: spice, wood or oak.

styles.name: Súmmum
styles.text: Made with at least 85 % of the principal grape varieties.

styles.name: Barrica
styles.text: Aged in oak barrels; spice, wood or oak aromas.

styles.name: Guarda
styles.text: Aged in wood, concrete or other non-steel tanks.

why.text: Slate and granite soils on sloping, often terraced vineyards meet a Mediterranean-oceanic climate. Godello comes out fresh and elegant.

styles.text: Godello whites and Mencía reds; also rosados, quality sparkling wine and Tostado, made from raisined grapes.

climate.text: Mediterranean-oceanic with Atlantic influence: cold winters, warm summers, mean 11 °C, 850 to 1,000 mm of rain.

soil.text: Five types: slate, limestone, granite, iron-rich clay and alluvial. Slate soils are shallow and stony.

altitude.text: The whole territory lies between 300 and 700 m.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow with green to amber tints; fruity, persistent. Reds: picota to ruby; red fruit; medium acidity. Tostado: yellow-gold or deep red; fruit, honey, caramel, raisin; sweet.

styles.name: Tostado
styles.text: Raisined grapes dried under cover for at least 30 days; naturally sweet.

styles.name: Producción controlada
styles.text: Stricter limits on yield per plot.

styles.name: Crianza
styles.text: Aged in oak barrels; fruit with barrel aromas.

styles.name: Gran Reserva
styles.text: Aged in oak barrels; spiced, with barrel aromas.

why.text: On the edge of where vines ripen. Big day-night swings slow ripening, so the grapes keep their natural freshness.

styles.text: Whites and reds, including Castes from the principal grapes. Also Barrica, quality sparkling wine and Tostado, a sweet wine from raisined grapes.

climate.text: Transition zone: temperate Mediterranean with Atlantic influence. Big day-night swings and little rain after fruit set.

soil.text: Rugged soils, mostly granite, with low water-holding capacity.

tastes.text: Whites: pale to golden yellow; ripe and fresh fruit, flowers, honey, herbs; fresh, balanced. Reds: violet red to cherry; red and black fruit, flowers; fresh, medium to high tannin. Tostado: amber to mahogany; sweet, long.

styles.name: Ribeiro Tostado
styles.text: Raisined-grape wine; amber to mahogany, honeyed, sweet and long.

styles.name: Ribeiro Castes
styles.text: Made from principal grapes; more complexity, structure and length.

why.text: Hot, dry summers and day-night swings of up to 30 degrees at ripening. Native grapes give aromatic, fresh, full-bodied wines.

styles.text: Whites, reds and rosados, usually drunk young. Barrica, crianza, reserva and gran reserva are aged versions.

climate.text: Temperate Mediterranean with a continental lean and Atlantic influence: hot dry summers, cold winters, swings up to 30 degrees at ripening.

soil.text: Slate and schist, granite and sand with low pH, and mixed sedimentary soils.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to gold; tree or tropical fruit. Reds: violet red to chestnut; red or black fruit. Rosés: pale pink to cherry; red or black fruit. All balanced in alcohol and acidity. Aged wines add spice or toast.

styles.name: Barrica, Crianza, Reserva, Gran Reserva
styles.text: Aged white or red; fruit with spice or toast.
